\subsection{\texttt{answer}}
\label{method:feedback_intelligence_agent.agent.FeedbackInsightAgent.answer}\index{Methods!answer}
Answer a user question using retrieved feedback as evidence.
\apifield{Usage}
\begin{lstlisting}[style=usage, language=Python]
answer(self, question: str, *, top_k: int = 4, history: Sequence[ConversationTurn] | None = None, filters: MetadataFilters | None = None) -> AgentAnswer
\end{lstlisting}
\apifield{Arguments}
\begin{arglist}
  \item[\texttt{question}] \texttt{str}, required.
  \item[\texttt{top\_\allowbreak{}k}] \texttt{int}, default \texttt{4}, keyword-only.
  \item[\texttt{history}] \texttt{Sequence[ConversationTurn]\allowbreak{} \textbar{} None}, default \texttt{None}, keyword-only.
  \item[\texttt{filters}] \texttt{MetadataFilters \textbar{} None}, default \texttt{None}, keyword-only.
\end{arglist}
\apifield{Value}\texttt{AgentAnswer}
\apifield{Details}Two deterministic guardrail gates protect the run: the input gate refuses unsafe questions before retrieval, and the context gate drops retrieved chunks carrying injection-style content before generation.

When \texttt{history} (previous conversation turns) is supplied, follow-up questions are first rewritten into standalone questions using the last turn, and the rewritten question drives routing, retrieval, and generation. The full history is never sent to retrieval. Without \texttt{history} the single-turn behaviour is unchanged.
\apifield{Source}\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}feedback\_\allowbreak{}intelligence\_\allowbreak{}agent/\allowbreak{}agent.\allowbreak{}py:101}~(\href{https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/feedback-intelligence-agent/blob/936886da072fa7025a57c5517b9c90772bedae09/src/feedback_intelligence_agent/agent.py#L101}{online})

\subsection{\texttt{chat}}
\label{method:feedback_intelligence_agent.agent.FeedbackInsightAgent.chat}\index{Methods!chat}
Answer a message inside a stored conversation and persist the turn.
\apifield{Usage}
\begin{lstlisting}[style=usage, language=Python]
chat(self, message: str, *, store: ConversationStore, conversation_id: str | None = None, top_k: int = 4, filters: MetadataFilters | None = None) -> tuple[AgentAnswer, str]
\end{lstlisting}
\apifield{Arguments}
\begin{arglist}
  \item[\texttt{message}] \texttt{str}, required.
  \item[\texttt{store}] \texttt{ConversationStore}, required, keyword-only.
  \item[\texttt{conversation\_\allowbreak{}id}] \texttt{str \textbar{} None}, default \texttt{None}, keyword-only.
  \item[\texttt{top\_\allowbreak{}k}] \texttt{int}, default \texttt{4}, keyword-only.
  \item[\texttt{filters}] \texttt{MetadataFilters \textbar{} None}, default \texttt{None}, keyword-only.
\end{arglist}
\apifield{Value}\texttt{tuple[AgentAnswer,\allowbreak{} str]\allowbreak{}}. The agent answer and the conversation identifier (newly generated when none was supplied).
\apifield{Details}Loads the conversation from \texttt{store} (or starts a new one when \texttt{conversation\_\allowbreak{}id} is \texttt{None}), answers with the previous turns as context, records the new turn (user message, answer, cited document IDs, route, and confidence), and saves the conversation back.
